overclaims: e1 explanation: "The study available on this date compares historical models, including April 2024 GPT-4 Turbo and early-2025 systems, on software and reasoning tasks. Its measured improvements in task length, error recovery, and tool use contradict little meaningful capability progress, while leaving returns per dollar unmeasured."
checks.note: The rationale and limitations match e1 (six-month doubling of time horizon, wide error bars, a different trend when only 2024 models are used, struggles on messy tasks). However, the published e1 explanation says the study includes April 2024 GPT-4 Turbo and measured gains in error recovery and tool use. None of that appears in the frozen excerpt or context. The cited excerpt "every six months" also drops "time horizon doubles", so on its own it does not say what is being measured.

The rationale, dates and limitations are supported, and the outcome matches the agreed assessment. However, the published citation excerpts drop wording that limits what the sources say. e1 omits "In Hard Prompt with Style Control", so it reads as an overall #1 ranking. e4 is the single word "behind", which drops "when it comes to software efficiency" and could read as DeepSeek being behind in general. e3 drops "The U.S. still leads". Each excerpt should include its qualifying wording.
